what_it_does: p-circuits propose a new way to design computer chips that blends analog (smooth, continuous electronics) and digital (exact on/off) approaches. Instead of converting between the two with expensive translators, p-circuits use a hybrid model: they keep digital inputs and outputs (standard binary signals) but process information through an analog function inside the chip. The output is random—like flipping a weighted coin—where the probability of being "1" depends on the analog function's output. This lets the chip do probabilistic computation (reasoning with uncertainty) without conversion overhead.
